\begin{align*} AB &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{20^2+25^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{1\,025} \\[5pt] &= 5\sqrt{41} \:\textrm{mm}. \end{align*}

In $\bigtriangleup AHB$ we have $\angle AHB = 90^\circ$, $AH=25\:\textrm{mm}$ and $BH=25\:\textrm{mm}.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

\begin{align*} AB &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{25^2+25^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{2\cdot 25^2} \\[5pt] &= 25\sqrt{2}\:\textrm{mm}. \end{align*}

question.explanation:
We use the triangle law of addition for $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$ We can start $\mathbf{a}$ from an arbitrary point on the plane. The resultant goes from the start of $\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $\mathbf{b}.$

Now, in $\bigtriangleup AHB$ we have $\angle AHB = 90^\circ$, $AH=30\:\textrm{mm}$ and $BH=20\:\textrm{mm}.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

\begin{align*} |\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}| &= AB \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{30^2+20^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{1\,300} \\[5pt] &= 10\sqrt{13}\:\textrm{mm}. \end{align*}
